messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@cloudforge.com>

Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace packaging options for CloudForge listing

Hi Olga / Lauren,

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. We kicked off an internal review and have two asks as we move toward publishing CloudForge on AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces:

1) Guidance on recommended SKU granularity (entry vs. standard vs. enterprise) per cloud. Our technical SKU currently bundles multi-region replication, private VPC peering, and dedicated inference pools — which feels heavy for an entry listing.
2) Co-sell certification path and any marketplace-specific checklist (especially Azure). Do we need separate certification artifacts per cloud or will a single package + platform attestations work?

We attached a first-pass SKU matrix (cloudforge-sku-proposal-v1.csv) and would appreciate your recommendation on how many SKUs to publish per cloud vs. a single multi-cloud SKU.

Target timeline: want to be live in US regions by end of May if possible. What constraints should we expect from your side (review time, co-sell enablement slots)?

Thanks,

Sarah Kim
Head of Cloud Partnerships | CloudForge
Attachments: cloudforge-sku-proposal-v1.csv (CSV stub, 12kb)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging options for CloudForge listing

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the kickoff and the SKU draft. Quick take below and a request for one more artifact.

Summary recommendation (high level):
- AWS: publish three SKUs (entry, standard, enterprise). Entry should strip out dedicated inference pools and VPC peering. Use usage-based pricing for entry to lower adoption friction.
- Azure: publish two SKUs (standard, enterprise) and use a toggle in the listing for "private deployment" upsell; Azure Marketplace tends to prefer fewer, clearer offers.
- GCP: single multi-region SKU is fine initially (standard) with an add-on SKU for dedicated capacity. GCP buyers accept add-ons more readily.

Key asks from Redwood for co-sell/cert:
- Can you provide a brief SOC2 summary page and network diagram (we need these for Azure certification).
- Please confirm which regions you want enabled (us-west-2, us-east-1, europe-west1 recommended for GA).

I've attached our co-sell checklist (co-sell_checklist.xlsx) — this outlines certification artifacts and partner enablement steps (partner intake -> publish -> co-sell training). Ben, can you confirm technical gating (regional GA / infra invariants) and whether we should block entry SKU from offering VPC peering?

Olga Petrov
Partner GTM Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: co-sell_checklist.xlsx (Excel stub, 40kb)

Hi all — quick technical callouts and constraints:

- Regional SKU gating: for GA we should only enable us-west-2 and us-east-1 for entry/standard; europe-west1 can be enabled for standard/enterprise after basic load testing. Region enablement requires image signing and region-specific infra smoke tests.

- VPC peering & private deployments: do not include VPC peering in the entry SKU. It needs network ops sign-off and a separate ticket for onboarding. Offer VPC peering as an add-on SKU (or a feature toggle that requires intake).

- Dedicated inference pools: enterprise-only and should be a separate SKU with reservation-based pricing. This lets us enforce capacity commitments and avoid noisy-neighbor risks.

- Azure certification: note that Azure Marketplace often requests a "manifest + ARM templates + security attestation" bundle. I attached azure-cert-requirements.pdf (stub) that lists common artifacts.

Proposed SKU mapping (short):
- Entry (AWS): usage-based, no VPC peering, no dedicated pools. Regions: us-west-2, us-east-1.
- Standard (AWS/Azure/GCP): includes multi-region, limited KV cache retention, standard support.
- Enterprise (all clouds): dedicated pools, VPC peering add-on, SLA 99.9%.
- Add-ons: VPC peering, Dedicated pool reservations, Extended retention.

I can spin up a small QA run for europe-west1 next week if we greenlight. Lauren — can you follow up on PMM copy for an Azure-friendly listing (fewer SKUs + clear add-ons)?

Ben Carter
Director Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachments: azure-cert-requirements.pdf (PDF stub, 85kb)

Thanks everyone — finalizing summary and next steps below so we have a single source of truth.

Decisions (approved):
- AWS: publish Entry / Standard / Enterprise. Entry excludes VPC peering and dedicated pools. Regions at launch: us-west-2, us-east-1.
- Azure: publish Standard / Enterprise. Standard will include a "Private deployment add-on" flow instead of a separate entry listing. Expect manifest + ARM bundle for Azure review.
- GCP: publish Standard (multi-region) + Dedicated-pools add-on SKU. Regions: northamerica-northeast1 (fallback) + us-west-2 initially.
